messages.subject: simulateData() and model-implied covariance?
parts:
so i know i can simulate data for my SEM model either going back to basics and using matrix algebra:
 
library(MASS)
L <- matrix(c(.7,0,.7,0,.7,0,.7,0,0,.7,0,.7,0,.7,0,.7), nrow=8, byrow=T)
PHI <- matrix(c(1,.3,.3,1), nrow=2, byrow=T)

PSI <- diag(8)

diag(PSI) <- 1-(.7)^2

Sigma <- L%*%PHI%*%t(L)+PSI
rownames(Sigma) <- paste("V", 1:nrow(Sigma), sep="")
colnames(Sigma) <- paste("V", 1:nrow(Sigma), sep="")

data_from_matrix <- as.data.frame(mvrnorm(500, c(rep(0,8)), Sigma))

or using lavaan:
 
library(lavaan)

model <- '
         f1 =~ .7*V1 + .7*V2 + .7*V3 + .7*V4
         f2 =~ .7*V5 + .7*V6 + .7*V7 + .7*V8
         
         f1 ~~ .3*f2
         f1 ~~ 1*f1
         f2 ~~ 1*f2
        
         V1 ~~ .51*V1
         V2 ~~ .51*V2
         V3 ~~ .51*V3
         V4 ~~ .51*V4
         V5 ~~ .51*V5
         V6 ~~ .51*V6
         V7 ~~ .51*V7
         V8 ~~ .51*V8 
         '
data_from_lavaan <- simulateData(model, 500)

and i know both data_from_lavaan and data_from_matrix will fit the same two-factor model with 8 indicators because they're using the same covariance matrix Sigma
 
Sigma
      V1    V2    V3    V4    V5    V6    V7    V8
V1 1.000 0.490 0.490 0.490 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147
V2 0.490 1.000 0.490 0.490 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147
V3 0.490 0.490 1.000 0.490 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147
V4 0.490 0.490 0.490 1.000 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147
V5 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147 1.000 0.490 0.490 0.490
V6 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.490 1.000 0.490 0.490
V7 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.490 0.490 1.000 0.490
V8 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.147 0.490 0.490 0.490 1.000

 
so, if i use the simulateData( ) function (i imagine) at some point lavaan grabs the appropriate coefficients, does all the matrix operations, comes up with the model-implied covariance matrix  and supplies that to some other R function (maybe mvrnorm( ) or something else) to generate data, am i correct?
 
if this is the general process, is there any way to extract the model-implied covariance that simulateData( ) will use to generate data? does it get stored someplace?
 
just trying to see if there is a short-cut to it instead of working on the matrix algebra from scratch every time. i prefer specifying structural equations than doing everything in matrix notation.
